title: Security & Change: The Power of Least Privilege

scenes.line1: Why is least privilege so critical?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why least privilege is the backbone of security? Let's break down why it's the single most important principle.

scenes.label: Baseline
scenes.sub: Every server starts with strict settings.
scenes.say: First, hardening means locking down every server with baseline settings. No unnecessary access, no open doors.
Least privilege is simple: only the rights you need, grouped for easy management, and access removed when no longer needed.
If someone gets in, least privilege keeps damage contained. Full access means a single breach can take down everything.

scenes.question: Should you grant root to make it easier?
scenes.right: No. Grant only the access needed for the task, like a sudo rule or group membership, and always document it.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap: never grant root or admin just to make things easier. Always limit access and document your decision.
